title: Personal Lattice KPI Notebook — Q4 Sprint
body:
Context and intent:
This is a personal scratchpad for a compact, experimental Q4 sprint focused on two axes: 1) consistent north-star progress and 2) rapid micro-experiments that move the needle on activation. Treat as my living lab: short, messy, pragmatic notes to myself. Not for productization yet — just signals, bets, and immediate next steps.

North star (one line):
Increase first-week activation for small-scale API adopters from 18% -> 28% within 8 weeks by removing three friction points and shipping two low-effort onboarding experiments.

Anchors (metrics I watch daily/3x-week):
- Signup -> successful call (first 24h): baseline 18% target 28%
- Average time to first successful call: baseline 2.1 days target <24h
- Docs run-rate: sessions/week per new user: baseline 0.8 target >=1.6

Objective A: Shorten time-to-first-success
KR A1: Reduce median time to first successful call from 2.1d to <24h
KR A2: Increase first-24h success rate from 12% to 25%
Micro-levers (hypotheses):
- H1: Add a one-click Postman collection + minimal API key demo reduces friction (expected uplift +6–8pp).
- H2: Add a tiny JS embed snippet in the quickstart (single line to paste) reduces time-to-first-call (expected -12h).
- H3: Send a targeted 1-minute onboarding email with example curl + test token improves conversion (+4pp).

Objective B: Improve early engagement with the console/docs
KR B1: Lift docs trial sessions per user from 0.8 to 1.6 in first week
KR B2: Raise feature-exploration (calls to embeddings or chat route) from 6% to 15%
Micro-levers:
- Quickstart analytics: add micro-goal checkboxes (I did X, I saw Y) to measure momentum and nudge next steps.
- Inline code toggles: show a tiny runnable example in docs that actually returns a predictable output — lower cognitive load.

Personal experiments and notes (running):
- Experiment X: Postman + one-click collection. Started 2026-01-10. Quick test with 12 users from devlist: success rate +7pp. Action: ship limited release behind feature flag.
- Experiment Y: 60-second onboarding email. Drafted subject lines A/B ("Your first API call in 60s" vs "Try Redwood in one minute"). Early CTR good, but open rates low. Need to retarget with a different time window.
- Experiment Z: JS embed snippet. Prototype shows big drop in time-to-first-call for web-native devs. Need to confirm for backend-focused cohort.

Retrospective (end of week ritual):
- What moved? Postman collection showed measurable lift quickly — low effort, high impact.
- What didn't? Email open rates are fickle; timing and subject need work.
- What surprised me? Backend folks prefer CLI/curl examples; web devs prefer a runnable snippet. Segmentation matters.

Signal thresholds (when to escalate):
- If first-24h success rate < 15% after two experiments -> escalate to roadmap: dedicate engineering cycle for onboarding flow.
- If median time to first call doesn't drop by 12h after two micro-releases -> run a 3-day usability study with 5 new signups.

Decision log (quick, timestamped):
- 2026-01-12: Roll Postman collection to feature-flagged users. Rationale: small lift in pilot.
- 2026-01-25: Pause wide email blast; focus on trigger-based messages based on 'signup time of day'.
- 2026-02-04: Add JS snippet to quickstart and instrument completion event.

Next actions (top 6, ordered):
1) Finalize Postman feature flag rollout and add telemetry to tag cohort (due 2026-02-03).
2) Create CLI-first quickstart variant for backend cohort (draft by 2026-02-07).
3) Run 5-session usability interview with backend devs (recruit via in-product prompt).
4) Rework 60-second email subject line copy and schedule A/B (target sent window: Tue 10am local).
5) Instrument 'runnable example executed' metric in docs (track as early engagement).
6) Quick sync with Sam Cho to align growth experiments and avoid duplicate emails.

Open questions / scribbles to revisit:
- Is the JS-snippet lowering signal quality (fake runs) vs real API adoption? Add a 'confirm' step to convert runnable-example runs to real calls.
- Where do we draw the boundary between product outreach and gated onboarding support?
- Can we tie mini-mentorship (15-min call) as a high-touch variant for high-value signups? Would that cannibalize automation?

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments < 2 engineering days where possible. Favor observable telemetry over vanity metrics.
- Document every small change in the decision log with date + outcome.
- Use the lattice metaphor: small beams (micro-experiments) that, when layered, create structural change.

Appendix (quick table):
Metric | baseline | current | target
---------------------------------
Signup->call 24h | 18% | 24% | 28%
Time to 1st call | 2.1d | 1.3d | <24h
Docs sessions/wk | 0.8 | 1.2 | 1.6
Feature exploration | 6% | 11% | 15%

End — lightweight, iterated weekly. Keep this doc messy; it helps me think.
